producer_report.summary: The generator and intro data now give a newcomer an introduction to Athena and the study before firstmate, which was the root cause of the 2/5 rating. The title and heading say 'Athena explains how firstmate handles work'. Two opening paragraphs say what Athena is, what a study is, and who made this one and why. The firstmate definition says its workers are AI coding agents, who uses it, and what problem it solves. When the pinned repository is on GitHub, the repository URL and every claim source link to the pinned commit's file and lines, and the link text is escaped. The glossary moved to after 'Why it is built this way'. A 'Next steps' section links to Athena and firstmate. Citation ids are smaller and muted. The captain entry is clarified, finding f2 is rewritten without internal field names, and the tests, design doc, README and CHANGELOG are updated. The full test suite passes, clippy is clean, and the site builds.

criteria_check.evidence: A new first item in intro.json 'what' defines firstmate. about.study defines a study.

open_issues: The 'why' sentence in about.study (Athena made the study to show it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it from sources) is my wording. The owner should confirm it matches the real reason.
The 'who uses it' and 'problem solved' wording in the firstmate definition is inferred from claims c1, c11, c21 and c22. The reviewer should check it is not an overstatement.
Next steps link to the repositories and tell readers to look at the README there for installing and trying. I did not check what the firstmate README says.
learnings: Study text outside the claims (about.athena, about.study) is rendered with no citations, since it makes no claim about firstmate.
